title: Microsoft Fabric Eventstreams Overview - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
summary: Microsoft Learn's conceptual overview of Fabric Eventstreams: a no-code capability to ingest events from a broad connector catalog (Event Hubs, IoT Hub, CDC sources, Kafka, cloud pub/sub services, Fabric/Azure native events), transform them in a drag-and-drop processor, and route them to destinations like Eventhouse, Lakehouse, or Activator.
audience: Data engineers and architects choosing how to bring streaming and change-data-capture sources into Fabric and deciding where transformation logic should live (in-stream vs. downstream engine).
why_it_matters: Eventstream is the ingestion and routing backbone for Fabric's real-time and event-driven scenarios, so its connector coverage, transformation model, and hard limits (message size, retention, delivery guarantees) directly bound what event-driven architectures are feasible on the platform.
takeaways: Eventstream exposes a large and growing connector catalog including Azure-native services, several database CDC connectors, generic Kafka/MQTT endpoints, and competing cloud streaming services (Kinesis, Google Pub/Sub, Confluent Cloud).
A no-code, drag-and-drop event processor supports transformations like filter, aggregate, group by, union, expand, and join, plus a preview SQL-based authoring option.
Whether transformations are available before all destinations depends on whether 'Enhanced capabilities' was enabled at eventstream creation time.
DeltaFlow (preview) converts raw CDC payloads into an analytics-ready tabular shape with automatic schema registration and destination table management.
Eventstream enforces firm operational limits: 1 MB max message size, 90-day max retention, and at-least-once delivery semantics.

claims.text: Eventstream is a no-code Fabric capability for bringing real-time events into the platform, transforming them, and routing them to one or more destinations, and it also exposes an Apache Kafka-compatible endpoint for producing or consuming events.

Eventstream's connector catalog spans Azure-native sources (Event Hubs, Event Grid, Service Bus, IoT Hub, Blob Storage events), several database change-data-capture connectors (Azure SQL, SQL Server on VM, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Oracle, Cosmos DB), generic protocol endpoints (Kafka, MQTT, HTTP), competing cloud streaming services (Amazon Kinesis, Amazon MSK, Google Cloud Pub/Sub, Confluent Cloud), and Fabric-native event types (workspace item events, OneLake events, job events, capacity events).

The Eventstream processor is a drag-and-drop, no-code editor supporting Filter, Manage fields, Aggregate, Group by, Union, Expand, and Join transformations, with an additional preview SQL operator for code-first stream processing logic including windowing and joins.

Whether an eventstream's no-code transformations are available for every destination, versus only for Lakehouse and Eventhouse destinations, depends on whether 'Enhanced capabilities' was enabled when the eventstream was created.

Eventstream can route the same event data to multiple destinations concurrently, including Eventhouse, Lakehouse, a Spark Notebook (preview) running Spark Structured Streaming, a custom endpoint, a derived stream, or Fabric Activator, without the destinations interfering with each other.
Routing an eventstream to an Eventhouse destination supports two ingestion modes: direct ingestion of raw events, or event processing before ingestion where transformations are applied first.

DeltaFlow (preview) is an Eventstream capability limited to specific CDC source connectors (Azure SQL, Azure SQL Managed Instance, SQL Server on VM, PostgreSQL) that converts raw change-data-capture payloads into an analytics-ready tabular shape, auto-registers schemas, and automatically creates and evolves matching destination tables as the source schema changes.
Creating a Fabric eventstream automatically provisions an underlying Azure Event Hubs namespace, which is what backs the eventstream's Kafka-compatible protocol endpoint.
Eventstream enforces a maximum message size of 1 MB, a maximum event data retention period of 90 days, and provides at-least-once event delivery guarantees.
Microsoft recommends running Fabric Eventstream on a capacity of at least F4 SKU size.

Derived eventstreams support pause and resume controls that let processing be temporarily halted and later resumed without affecting other inputs or outputs on the same eventstream, and select sources/destinations support Workspace Private Link for private network connectivity.
